findings.where: Nav bar (the gummed binding), the logo at top left, desktop and phone
findings.fault: The logo has been recoloured. The aqueduct mark and the MMM INFRA wordmark are drawn in pale cream on the binding red, so the logo's own grey arches and blue Georgia wordmark (#404040, #0070C0) appear nowhere on the page. The palette also never lists the logo colours, either as tokens with a job or as logo-only.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo the brief says must stay unchanged. Visitors who know MMM Infra's blue-and-grey mark from his current site and LinkedIn would not recognise this one as the same practice.

findings.where: Hero, the 'write to me' margin note (the only call to action), desktop
findings.fault: The page's one call to action is a small rotated script note out in the left margin, outside the column the eye follows down the page. The heading, the clipped photo and the large aqueduct sketch all outweigh it, so it comes last when you squint. Apart from the nav's 'Contact', it is the only way to reach Mark.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has read the hero and wants to get in touch, but has to search for the way to do it. Mark too, because getting in touch is the one job the homepage has.

findings.where: Whole page: the hero and the missing footer
findings.fault: Mark's email address never appears in full as link text. The only routes are a mailto link behind the words 'write to me' and the nav's 'Contact'. The palette names a footer for the binding colour, but no footer is drawn.
findings.who_objects: A procurement officer who wants to copy the address into their own mail system or a shortlist, and cannot see it without clicking.

findings.where: Article specimen, the lecture row 'Streamlining the PPP Process…', and the motion sketch's 'Replay the note'
findings.fault: The link and button signs are swapped. The lecture link is set in the same bold navy Caslon as the static palette labels ('Pad', 'Ballpoint') and the table headings, with no underline. 'Replay the note' is a button but wears the prose-link underline. The lecture row's bottom rule also runs through the descenders of its last line, so on the phone it reads as an underline on just that line.
findings.who_objects: A reader of an article page who doesn't notice that the lecture title opens the PDF. Angélique, who will copy this row style for every new publication.

findings.where: Hero, the italic line 'Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience.'
findings.fault: Standing is claimed with a size word (a count of years) and not shown through checkable work. This line takes the hero's second place, right under the World Bank fact.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank selection panel, which judges a consultant by project type, region and role, not by years. To them it reads as a firm's boast, which also cuts against Mark's 'no big-firm claims' value.

findings.where: Article specimen headline 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' (desktop), and the handwritten pull quote (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: Headings and the pull quote snap to every second ruled line, which leaves a full blank line between their lines. The desktop article title breaks after 'Public-' with a wide gap before 'Private', and the quote reads as loose separate lines. The hero h1 is set solid, and the phone's article title is set tight, so like headings are spaced differently.
findings.who_objects: Any reader of an article page, who reads the title and the quote in broken pieces. The layout round would inherit two different heading rhythms.

findings.where: Small captions throughout the tile (the palette notes, the texture caption, the type-pair notes, the motion sketch's easing and total lines)
findings.fault: 16 px captions sit on the 32 px rules, so they look double-spaced and fall apart into lines. The motion table's cells beside them use tighter leading that ignores the rules, so small text has two rhythms.
findings.who_objects: Angélique and the next round, who need one caption style to copy. A reader sees loose, uneven small text.

findings.where: Pad margin, the vertical double line down the left, desktop and phone
findings.fault: The margin line is drawn in a dark olive-brown, not the red the direction card and the palette's 'Margin red: margin, note' give it. The one cue that says 'legal pad' is lost, and the red is left to the note alone.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who asked for the legal pad: without its red margin line, the yellow ruled page reads as a generic notebook.

findings.where: Article specimen, the pull quote set in Nanum Pen Script
findings.fault: The type pair says Mark's hand appears once per view, as the margin call to action. The article specimen also uses it for a pull quote, so a real article page would show the hand twice.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who will be adding posts and needs to know when the handwriting may be used. Its effect as Mark's one personal note weakens if it repeats.

findings.fault: The two navies for type and for asides and hatching are too close to tell apart and too far apart to be one colour. On the page, asides look like the same ink slightly off, not a deliberate second rank.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader, and the layout round: the asides would look like a printing slip, not a second rank.
